build_matrix_r124.self_reference_constraint: An immutable committed file cannot contain the SHA of the commit that contains it: the SHA is a hash over a tree that includes this file, so writing the value in would change it. Therefore every SHA in this file is either the stable BASE or a PRIOR TIP. The exact current head, its parent and its tree are attested in the PR #28 BODY, which is mutable metadata and does not alter any git SHA. Reviewers verify the live tip with `gh api repos/BradleyGleavePortfolio/tgp-agent-context/pulls/28 --jq .head.sha` cross-checked against `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/docs/op75-p0-audit-5076a07a`. No in-file claim to pin the current head is made, because any such claim would be false by construction.
build_matrix_r124._pr_28_reviewed_input_head_rename_note_s: KEY RENAMED AT THE SIXTH PASS (R5/R132). The prior key name was `pr_28_head`, which read as the CURRENT head of PR #28. It never was: its value is the capture-time tip `5c2f0057cd0ba4f5cba3b2dd2e6e718927549650`, the exact ctxrepo head the independent reviews of the audit reports examined. Remediation commits have landed since - count them with `git rev-list --count 5c2f0057cd0ba4f5cba3b2dd2e6e718927549650..HEAD` rather than reading a number here - so a reader resolving `pr_28_head` against the live PR would see a mismatch and could read it as R124 drift or INFRA_DEATH. Renamed to `pr_28_reviewed_input_head`, which says what the value is. The OLD NAME IS NOT RETAINED AS A DATA KEY because retaining a misleading name is the defect, not the remedy; it is preserved here in this note per R5/R132 instead. No consumer breaks: the old key was read by no script, workflow or prose in this repository - verified with `grep -rn pr_28_head`, which returns only prose notes such as this one, never a data key. CORRECTED AT THE SEVENTH PASS (R5/R132): this sentence previously said the sweep 'returns only this note', singular, while the rename is recorded in more than one note and the sweep therefore returns several - DECISION_LOG.md already stated it correctly in the plural. Assert the structural property instead of the grep count: jq '[paths|.[-1]|strings|select(.==$k)]|length' --arg k pr_28_head returns 0 on every mirror, which is the claim that actually matters. THE CANONICAL R124 BLOCK IS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: lines 3-8 of both audit reports still read `- PR #28 head:` because that six-line block is md5-pinned at 0afb8191a6f59807bc9fc1aef39d68a2 and is the sole canonical family; editing its label would break the pin for no safety gain. The canonical block is a CAPTURE-TIME record and is correct as such; this file is a labelled non-canonical mirror, so it is the surface that can afford a clearer key name. The VALUES remain byte-identical between canonical block and mirror - only the mirror's key name differs, and that divergence is recorded here so it is not mistaken for drift.
